title: Shadow E1: at iso-FLOPs on a 0.06-0.21M-param char LM, a weight-tied looped block loses to plain depth
hypothesis: At matched training FLOPs on tiny natural-language data (<=0.25M params), a weight-tied block looped k times does NOT beat an untied k-layer stack - at this scale the extra parameters of untied depth buy more than the extra iterations of a shared block. Deliberate falsification target for Shadow's core mechanism.
question: Does Shadow's weight-tied looped block pay for itself against plain untied depth at iso-FLOPs on natural-language data at <=0.25M params, where Ouro/recurrent-depth have never been controlled?
method: nanoGPT-style pre-norm decoder-only char LM (d=64, 4 heads, FFN 256, ctx 64, vocab 65) on tiny-shakespeare, 90/10 split. For k in {1,2,4}: tied = ONE block applied k times (49.7k block params at every k); untied = k distinct blocks applied once each. Both do k block applications, hence identical fwd/bwd FLOPs per step. All 12 runs share 2200 steps, batch 16x64 tokens (~2.25M tokens), AdamW lr 2e-3 (100-step warmup, cosine to 10%), wd 0.1, clip 1.0, identical init and batch stream; 2 seeds per condition. Metric: val bits/char on a fixed 40-batch val set. Built-in check: tied-k1 and untied-k1 are the same model and must be bit-identical (gap = 0.0).
architecture: decoder-only transformer char LM, d_model 64, 4 heads, FFN 256, ctx 64; tied (1 block x k) vs untied (k blocks); 62k params (tied, all k) vs 62k/112k/211k params (untied k=1/2/4)

result_summary: Hypothesis supported. At iso-FLOPs the weight-tied loop never beats untied depth and the penalty grows monotonically with k: +0.0377 bpc at k=2, +0.0790 bpc at k=4, with the tied and untied seed distributions fully separated at both k. Stronger still, looping is worse than not looping: tied-k4 spends 4x the FLOPs of tied-k1 at identical parameter count and ends 0.083 bpc worse. Shadow's looped block cannot be justified on tiny-scale LM loss; it must earn its ledger entry on test-time-compute or extrapolation axes instead. Honest caveats: undertrained (all curves still descending at 2200 steps, ~2.79 bpc absolute), iso-hyperparameter rather than per-condition-tuned LR, and a VANILLA loop with no per-iteration input injection or per-loop LayerNorm.

title: Does the Game-of-Life capacity window transfer to language? Tied vs untied recursion across width

title: Shadow E3: entropy-based adaptive exit on a tiny looped char LM - no better than a coin flip at matched compute
hypothesis: On a weight-tied looped char LM (max k=4, ~0.06M params) trained with per-loop deep supervision, an inference-time per-token entropy exit traces a better val-bits/char vs mean-loops/token frontier than fixed loop counts, i.e. adaptive halting saves compute without hurting loss by spending loops only on high-entropy tokens. The competing prediction (TRM critique 2512.11847) is that it collapses to a fixed depth because loops past the first buy almost nothing at this scale.
question: Does Ouro-style entropy halting recover any of the loss that the plain tied loop takes at iso-FLOPs (registry id 2026-07-25_shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop), by allocating loops only where they are needed?
method: One pre-norm decoder block (d=64, 4 heads, d_ff 256, ctx 64, vocab 65) weight-tied and applied up to k_max=4 times, LM head readable after any loop; 62,272 params. Four models x 2 seeds, identical hyperparameters (1800 steps, batch 16, AdamW lr 2e-3, 100-step warmup + cosine, wd 0.1, clip 1.0): fixed_k1/k2/k4 (CE on the final loop only) and deepsup_k4 (CE averaged over readouts after loops 1..4). Three inference-time policies swept on deepsup_k4 over the SAME 51,200 fixed val tokens: (i) fixed k in {1,2,3,4}; (ii) entropy exit - after loop i a token with predictive entropy <= tau halts, its hidden state freezes but still serves as a key/value, 15 thresholds tau in [0, 6.1] bits; (iii) random exit - compute-matched control where each active token halts with probability p, p solved numerically so mean loops/token matches each entropy point. Metric: val bits/char vs mean loops/token, plus a FLOP-honest axis charging the entropy probe for its per-loop LM-head evaluation (7.8% of a block). Ablation: entropy exit on the non-deep-supervised fixed_k4 model.
architecture: weight-tied looped decoder-only transformer, k_max=4, d_model 64, 62.3k params, per-loop LM readout

metrics.headline: entropy halting never beats fixed depth (best interior point +0.0005 bpc for a 1% compute saving; +0.021 bpc at a 39% saving) and is statistically indistinguishable from a compute-matched RANDOM exit above 3.4 loops/token, becoming strictly worse than random below it (+0.0058 / +0.0116 bpc at 39% / 61% savings); loops 2-3 are used by <6% of tokens at any threshold

result_summary: Hypothesis refuted, honest negative. Every entropy operating point sits on or above the fixed-k frontier of the same model: the best interior point is +0.0005 bits/char for a 1% compute saving, and a real saving costs real loss (+0.0072 / +0.0150 / +0.0212 bpc at 15% / 27% / 39% fewer loops). The decisive control is the compute-matched RANDOM exit: above 3.4 loops/token entropy is within +-0.0007 bpc of coin-flipping (inside the 0.003 seed spread) and below it entropy is strictly WORSE than random (+0.0022/+0.0058/+0.0116 bpc at 2.93/2.44/1.56 loops), so the entropy signal carries no usable information about which tokens need more depth. The policy does collapse, but to MAXIMUM depth rather than the shallow collapse the TRM critique predicts: at any threshold costing under 0.001 bpc, >=96% of tokens still run all four loops (char-level Shakespeare is a ~2.9 bits/char target, so almost nothing looks easy), and loops 2 and 3 are used by <6% of tokens at any threshold, i.e. the mechanism degenerates into a binary 1-or-4 easy/hard split rather than graded allocation. The upstream reason is that there is nothing to allocate: the deep-supervised model's quality-vs-depth curve is nearly flat and non-monotone (k1 2.9488, k2 2.9123, k3 2.9103, k4 2.9203) and the separately trained fixed-k models get monotonically worse with more loops (2.8556 / 2.8912 / 2.9350 at k=1/2/4), so the globally best point in the experiment is the dedicated k=1 model - fewest loops AND lowest bpc. Two side results: deep supervision is a hard prerequisite (naive entropy exit on the non-deep-supervised k4 model degrades 2.935 -> 3.837 bpc) but is not free (its k=1 readout is 0.093 bpc worse than a dedicated k=1 model, exactly where you would want to exit); and FLOP-honest accounting charges the entropy probe 7.8% of a block per loop, putting its zero-exit operating point at 4.31 loop-equivalents, i.e. above fixed k=4. Caveats: 1800 steps at 0.06M params is an early-training iso-compute regime (2.85-2.95 bpc, far from converged), one task, 2 seeds, inference-time exit only, and mean loops/token is a compute proxy - no wall-clock saving is claimed.

title: TRM at nano scale: the outer refinement loop is the whole story, the inner latent recursion is not
hypothesis: At ~0.1M params on 4x4 Sudoku, TRM-style recursion (arXiv:2510.04871) buys accuracy mainly through the OUTER refinement loop (repeatedly re-encoding a full candidate solution) rather than through INNER latent recursion at matched core-block applications; and per the TRM critique (arXiv:2512.11847) most of the achievable full-puzzle solve rate is already present at recursion depth 1.
question: When you split TRM recursion into its two halves and hold parameters and core-block applications exactly equal, which half buys generalization - and does solve rate saturate at recursion depth 1?
method: One 2-layer MLP core (LN -> 256x192 -> GELU -> 192x256) on a flat 256-d state (16 cells x 16-d), applied exactly T times in three arms that differ ONLY in the information path between steps: (a) outer_deepsup - state passes through the 16x4 answer distribution, re-embedded, CE loss at every step; (a') outer_finalsup - same loop, CE at the final step only (deep-supervision control); (b) inner_latent - state is the full-width 256-d latent z (z <- z + core(x+z)), decoded once at the end. T=1 is the single-pass baseline where all arms collapse to one core application. Identical param count (116,624) everywhere; full backprop through the loop (no TRM 1-step gradient approximation). Depths T in {1,2,4,8}, 3 seeds, 24 runs. 1200 steps, batch 128, AdamW lr 3e-3 (40-step warmup + cosine), wd 0.01, grad-clip 1.0; every run reaches 1.000 solve rate on the training puzzles, so this compares generalization at converged train fit.
architecture: TRM-style weight-tied 2-layer MLP recursion, 116,624 params, 16-cell flat state, T in {1,2,4,8} core applications

dataset.name: synthetic 4x4 Sudoku; all 288 valid grids enumerated, split by SOLUTION GRID into 202 train / 86 held-out; puzzles are 4-8-given maskings rejection-sampled for a unique solution (2000 train, 800 held-out-grid test, 800 seen-grid unseen-mask test; mean 9.15 blanks)

task: 4x4 Sudoku completion (constraint satisfaction); metrics on blank cells only
compute: CPU single-threaded, 398.8s for all 24 runs

metrics.headline: at matched compute the outer answer-space refinement loop scales (0.220 -> 0.513 solve rate, T=1 -> 8) while inner latent recursion is flat (0.218 -> 0.245); +0.268 solve rate for outer over inner at T=8; deep supervision is NOT the cause (final-step-only supervision is better, 0.550); the critique's '94% at recursion step 1' holds for latent recursion (89%) and fails for the refinement loop (40-43%)

result_summary: Hypothesis confirmed on the mechanism, refuted on the saturation claim - and the two results are the same finding seen from two sides. Splitting TRM recursion into mutually exclusive information paths through one identical 116k-param core at exactly matched core-block applications: the OUTER refinement loop (state passes through the 16x4 answer distribution) climbs 0.220 -> 0.339 -> 0.448 -> 0.513 held-out-grid solve rate at T=1/2/4/8, while INNER latent recursion (full-width 256-d z, decoded once) is essentially flat at 0.218 -> 0.245 over the same 8x compute, a +0.268 gap at T=8 with per-cell seed std <= 0.030. Latent depth is not merely useless: its held-out cell accuracy DECREASES with depth (0.760 -> 0.737) while its seen-grid solve rate rises 0.533 -> 0.722, i.e. extra latent recursion buys memorization capacity rather than constraint propagation. TRM-style deep supervision is not the cause of the outer loop's win - supervising only the final step is better (0.550 vs 0.513 at T=8, and 0.409 vs 0.339 at T=2). The TRM critique's '94% of performance at recursion step 1' therefore splits by which recursion is ablated: fraction of best-depth solve rate already present at T=1 is 0.89 for inner latent (claim roughly holds) but only 0.40-0.43 for the outer refinement loop (claim refuted). Caveats: one task, a 16-cell CSP with only 288 total solutions, 1200 steps, and the outer curve is still rising at T=8 so its saturation point was not found.

title: nano-Coconut on DAG reachability: continuous thoughts need the curriculum, still lose to discrete CoT, and are not a BFS frontier
hypothesis: At ~0.1M params on yes/no DAG reachability, Coconut-style continuous thoughts (arXiv:2412.06769; H=3 latent steps, each the model's own last hidden state fed back as the next input embedding) beat discrete chain-of-thought and no-CoT at matched parameters and matched training steps, and a per-node linear probe on the thought vectors decodes the BFS frontier well above a shuffled-label control.
question: At nano scale and matched compute, do continuous latent thoughts beat discrete CoT, pause tokens and no-CoT on multi-hop graph reachability - and does each thought actually carry the BFS frontier, once you control for random features and for the representation that exists BEFORE any thought?
method: One 2-layer pre-norm decoder-only transformer (d_model=64, 4 heads, FFN 256, learned absolute positions, 103,168 params) trained in five arms that differ ONLY in what occupies the 3 slots between the query and the answer: (a) nocot - nothing, answer CE only; (b) pause - 3 learned <pause> tokens, answer CE only (filler-token control); (c) cot - 3 supervised discrete hop tokens (shortest path for positives, greedy dead-end walk for negatives), CE on every hop token plus the answer, greedily DECODED at eval rather than teacher-forced; (d) coconut - 3 continuous thoughts under the paper's staged curriculum (k=0->1->2 latents over the first 60% of steps, then k=3), full backprop through the thought chain; (e) coconut_nocur - k=3 from step 0, no curriculum. pause/cot/coconut* use identical token positions and identical transformer-block applications. Identical params, optimiser, batch size and 1100 training steps everywhere; batch 64, AdamW lr 2e-3 (50-step warmup), wd 0.01, grad-clip 1.0, 2 seeds, 10 runs. Novel angle: per-node logistic probes on the hidden state at each slot predicting the BFS frontier F_k={v:dist(src,v)=k} and reach set R_k={v:1<=dist(src,v)<=k}, macro AUC over the 8 node columns on 1200 train / 1000 held-out probe graphs from disjoint seeds, against THREE reference points - a shuffled-label control, an untrained random-init model, and slot 0 (the query-position hidden, before any thought).

result_summary: Half confirmed, half refuted, and the refuted half is the interesting one. On accuracy the mechanism is real: at 103k params and 1100 matched training steps, Coconut-style continuous thoughts reach 0.873 held-out accuracy vs 0.600 for no-CoT (+0.273) and 0.687 for a compute-matched pause-token control (+0.186), so the gain is not merely extra forward passes - the content fed back matters. But the curriculum is load-bearing: dropped in cold (k=3 from step 0), continuous thoughts score 0.547, WORSE than doing nothing, answering YES on 75% of negatives; the curriculum is worth +0.326. And discrete supervised CoT still wins outright at 0.937 (-0.064 for Coconut), getting there by a different route: cot is near-perfect on negatives (0.990) and 1-hop (0.994) but DEGRADES with depth (0.894 -> 0.768), while coconut IMPROVES with depth (0.821 -> 0.884 -> 0.934) and pays on negatives (0.865). The novel probe angle returns an honest negative. The BFS frontier F_k is linearly decodable from the k-th continuous thought at 0.796/0.721/0.729 macro AUC, which crushes the shuffled-label control (0.495/0.496/0.507) - the comparison the backlog asked for, and it passes. But an UNTRAINED randomly-initialised network scores 0.734/0.723/0.727, so the trained thoughts' lift over generic random features is only +0.062/-0.002/+0.002; and the hidden state at the query position BEFORE any thought decodes the frontier strictly better (0.893/0.766/0.811), with the reach-set AUC falling monotonically down the thought chain (R_1: 0.89 -> 0.80 -> 0.74 -> 0.73). The probe machinery is validated by the cot model scoring AUC 1.000 for F_1 at slot 0, exactly as it must. The one positive probe finding: training WITH thoughts makes the pre-thought representation far more frontier-decodable than training without (coconut 0.893 vs nocot 0.598 vs untrained 0.734 for F_1). So whatever the thoughts carry that lifts accuracy from 0.60 to 0.87, it is not a linearly readable BFS frontier - the chain appears to compress toward the yes/no decision rather than maintain an explicit search state, contra the hand-built superposition construction of arXiv:2505.12514. Caveats: one task, one graph size, 2 seeds, 1100 steps with no arm trained to convergence (cot and coconut were both still improving), a linear probe only, and a fixed-width adjacency-slot graph encoding rather than a free-order edge list - the latter left every arm at chance inside the time-box.

title: Grokking (a+b) mod 59: spectral-entropy collapse LAGS the test-accuracy jump; only restricted loss leads
hypothesis: A 1-layer LayerNorm-free transformer trained full-batch on a fraction of (a+b) mod 59 will memorize fast and generalize late (grokking), and the spectral entropy of its token-embedding matrix will COLLAPSE measurably BEFORE the test-accuracy jump - making it a predictive online progress measure competitive with Nanda's restricted/excluded loss.
question: Does spectral-entropy collapse actually LEAD the grokking transition, or merely describe the grokked state - and how does it compare head-to-head against restricted/excluded loss on the same runs?
method: 1-layer transformer (no LayerNorm, no biases) on [a, b, '='], logits read at the last position only; full-batch AdamW (lr 1e-3, weight decay 1.0, betas 0.9/0.98), seed 0. Train-fraction sweep 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.3 of the 3481 pairs with per-run wall-clock caps (150/360/90 s). Four progress measures tracked every 50 steps: H_fourier (entropy of the DFT power spectrum of W_E down the token axis, DC dropped), H_svd (entropy of the normalized singular-value energy spectrum of W_E), H_cov (entropy of the penultimate-representation covariance eigenspectrum - the arXiv:2604.13123 measure, reimplemented), and Nanda restricted/excluded loss (logits over the full p x p grid, centered over the output axis, 2D-DFT'd over (a,b), split on the FINAL model's key frequencies and replayed against periodic in-RAM checkpoints). Lead time is measured from the MEMORIZATION step (train acc >= 0.99), comparing when each measure completes 50% of its post-memorization movement against when test accuracy crosses 0.5. Two controls: (a) the same primary run re-analysed as if training had STOPPED at the jump, isolating the normalization artifact; (b) a train_frac 0.3 run that memorizes but never leaves the plateau, giving a false-positive rate.
architecture: 1-layer attention+MLP transformer, no LayerNorm, d_model 64, 4 heads, d_mlp 256, vocab 60, 56,960 params

dataset.name: all 59^2 = 3481 (a,b) pairs of (a+b) mod 59; deterministic random splits at train_frac 0.5 (1740/1741), 0.4 (1392/2089), 0.3 (1044/2437)

metrics.headline: p=59, train_frac 0.5 groks fully (memorized step 220, test acc 50% at step 862, delay 642 steps, final test acc 1.000, 6 frequencies holding 90.5% of embedding power); but every spectral entropy LAGS the jump (H_fourier -936, H_svd -876, H_cov -571 steps, only 14-25% of their collapse done at test-acc 50%) while only Nanda's restricted/excluded loss leads (+351 / +562). Re-analysing the SAME run as if stopped at the jump flips all three entropies positive (+298 / +386 / +146), showing the published lead is a normalization artifact of truncated training; and on a train_frac 0.3 run that never generalizes (test acc 0.028 vs chance 0.017) H_svd still falls 0.98 bits, a false positive.

result_summary: Hypothesis refuted, with a mechanism for why the opposite is reported. The classic grokking curve reproduces cleanly at 57k params on (a+b) mod 59 in 2.5 minutes of CPU: train acc 0.99 at step 220, test acc 50% at step 862 (grok delay 642 steps), test acc 1.000 by step ~3000, and the grokked model is unambiguously Fourier - 6 frequencies hold 90.5% of the embedding power and H_fourier falls 4.85 -> 2.90 bits (28.8 -> 7.5 effective frequencies). The delay is governed by data: 642 steps at train_frac 0.5, 11,021 steps at 0.4 (still only 0.524 when the 360s cap hit), and no generalization at all at 0.3. On the only fully-grokked run, however, all three spectral entropies LAG the test-accuracy jump - H_fourier -936, H_svd -876, and H_cov -571 steps - having completed just 14-25% of their collapse at the moment test accuracy already reaches 50%. Only Nanda's restricted loss (+351 steps, monotone, 84% complete at the jump) and excluded loss (+562, but non-monotone with a 6.4x overshoot) genuinely fire early, and neither is causally available online because both require the FINAL model's key frequencies. Two controls explain the discrepancy with the published +1020-step claim: (1) re-analysing the SAME primary run as if training had stopped at the jump flips every entropy from lagging to leading (H_fourier -936 -> +298, H_svd -876 -> +386, H_cov -571 -> +146), because normalizing by 'fraction of total movement' while the denominator is still growing manufactures a lead - our own truncated train_frac 0.4 run reports fake leads of +4727 to +9466 for exactly this reason; (2) on the train_frac 0.3 run that memorizes but never leaves chance (test acc 0.028 vs chance 0.017 after 4388 steps), H_svd still falls 0.98 bits and H_fourier 0.12 bits with only 35.9% of power in the top 6 frequencies, i.e. entropy collapse fires without any generalization. H_cov, the published measure, was also the noisiest signal tracked (swinging 2.4-4.8 bits between adjacent evals) and moved the wrong way (+0.48 bits) in the null control. Net: at this scale there is no cheap ONLINE progress measure that both leads the jump and stays silent when the model never groks. Caveats: one seed, one modulus, one architecture, all runs wall-clock capped, and the prior work used p=97/d=128/train_frac 0.20 - a much longer plateau than fits a 10-minute box - so the sign of the lead may be regime-dependent.

title: The probe can lie: at matched 99%+ linear-probe accuracy, top-of-stack type costs 5.31 excess nats to erase and depth parity costs less than a random direction
hypothesis: In a 27k-param 2-layer 1-head transformer trained to next-token-predict Dyck-2 bracket sequences, several stack state variables (exact nesting depth, depth parity, second-from-top bracket type, top-of-stack recency) will be linearly decodable at well-above-chance accuracy while carrying near-zero CAUSAL effect on the model's predictions, whereas the variables the next-token decision provably requires (top-of-stack bracket type, the depth>0 indicator, current-token identity) will be both decodable AND causally load-bearing - i.e. probe accuracy is not evidence of use.
question: Per candidate feature, how far apart are linear decodability and causal use in a model whose ground-truth algorithm is known exactly - and does a null causal effect survive an erasure that is CERTIFIED to have removed the feature?
method: 2-layer 1-head pre-norm decoder (d_model 32, d_ff 128, learned absolute positions, 27,200 params) trained 2000 steps (AdamW lr 3e-3, batch 96, wd 0.01, 100-step warmup) on next-token prediction over seeded Dyck-2 strings (2 bracket types, 10-20 pairs = 22-42 tokens, max depth 10, p_open 0.6, mean depth 3.51). Whole pipeline repeated for seeds 0 and 1. Behaviour measured on a fixed 1200-sequence / 37,074-position eval set with four metrics: next-token CE (all positions, depth-0 positions, closer-target positions), close-type accuracy (is the correct closer scored above the wrong one - provably a function of top-of-stack type), and illegal-close probability mass at depth-0 positions (provably a function of depth>0). Seven candidate features per position (top_type, depth_gt0, depth_exact 11-way, depth_parity, second_type, top_recency restricted to closer positions, cur_tok_is_open) are probed with linear probes at two residual-stream sites (resid_mid after block 1, resid_final after block 2), split BY SEQUENCE, 20k train / 8k test positions, each paired with a shuffled-label probe. Causal use is measured by closed-form LEACE erasure (Belrose et al. 2306.03819) fitted at the site, h -> mu + (h-mu)A^T, which guarantees linear guardedness; guardedness is VERIFIED by refitting a fresh probe on the erased activations. Controls: 12 random rank-matched erasers of identical form per (site, rank) - variance-matched by construction because LEACE works in whitened space - plus a same-rank shuffled-label eraser; every causal effect is reported as excess over the random-eraser mean, in sd units. Pre-registered verdict rule: decodable = probe beats majority by >=0.05; causally used = >=0.05 excess nats AND z>=2 on at least one CE slice. Entanglement diagnostics: pairwise Cramer's V between feature labels and cosine of the smallest principal angle between erased subspaces.
architecture: 2-layer, 1-head pre-norm decoder-only transformer, d_model 32, d_ff 128, learned absolute PE, 27,200 params

metrics.headline: depth_parity probes at 0.995 (majority 0.519, shuffled-label control 0.515) at resid_final and is linearly guarded after rank-1 LEACE erasure (refit probe 0.519 vs majority 0.519), yet the best-case erasure damage over rank-matched random erasers is only -0.161 nats (z=-0.8) and -0.023 close-type accuracy - versus +5.314 nats for top_type.

result_summary: Hypothesis confirmed for the headline feature, with two honest misses. The 27k-param model learns the task cleanly (close-type accuracy 0.9994, illegal-close mass at depth 0 0.0010 down from 0.26 at init, next-token CE 0.874 nats; the residual CE is irreducible because the generator's open/close choice is stochastic). At the final residual stream, two features are read out at essentially identical linear-probe accuracy and behave completely differently under a certified erasure: top-of-stack TYPE probes at 0.999 and its rank-1 LEACE erasure costs +5.31 excess nats on closer targets (z=+13.6), dropping close-type accuracy by 0.640 (0.999 -> 0.359, below chance) - it is a single direction holding 76% of the residual variance; depth PARITY probes at 0.995 against a 0.519 majority (shuffled-label probe 0.515) and its rank-1 erasure - verified linearly guarded, refit probe 0.5188 vs majority 0.5188 - costs -0.16 nats, i.e. LESS damage than a random rank-matched direction, in both seeds (-0.156, -0.165), with close-type accuracy and illegal-close mass unmoved. That null is structural and pre-statable: in any Dyck prefix depth(t) = t (mod 2), so parity is decodable for free from the positional embedding while carrying zero information about the answer. depth_exact tells the same story at higher selectivity (probe 0.896 vs 0.160 majority, Pearson r 0.962) but its rank-10 erasure necessarily deletes the depth>0 predicate too (Cramer's V = 1.0), so its positive is inherited; on all-position CE it scores -0.52 excess nats and it IMPROVES close-type accuracy by 0.12 over a random rank-10 eraser. second_type (probe 0.628) is also decodable-but-unused (+0.01 nats). Role specialisation is clean: top_type's erasure damages only the closer-target CE slice, depth_gt0's only the depth-0 slice (+1.48 nats, z=+3.2) - and depth_gt0 looks inert (+0.03 nats) if you average over all positions, so averaging over the wrong positions would have falsely declared a genuinely-used feature unused. All 7 features at resid_final were certified linearly guarded in both seeds (refit probe exactly at the majority baseline), so the nulls are not weak-ablation artifacts. Two misses against the pre-registered expectations: top_recency was predicted unused but scores +1.17 nats (z=+3.2) in both seeds - its labels are near-independent of every other feature (Cramer's V <= 0.13) but its erased direction overlaps the cur_tok_is_open subspace at cos 0.62, i.e. collateral damage rather than use; and cur_tok_is_open was predicted used but comes in at +0.36 nats, z=+0.8, under-powered rather than clearly null. Net: at matched probe accuracy, decodability and causal use are unrelated (+5.31 vs -0.16 excess nats), erasure evidence is asymmetric (a null is strong, a positive can be entanglement), and the shuffled-label probe control - which every feature here passes - certifies only that the probe is not memorising and says nothing about use. Caveats: 2 seeds, one architecture, one depth regime; this is a replication of arXiv:2604.22128 with a certified-erasure and ground-truth-null methodology added, not a new finding.

title: KAN on Feynman I.12.2: Coulomb's law recovered EXACTLY (exponent error 0.006), but the sample-efficiency claim is refuted - the KAN is 2.8x worse than an iso-param MLP at n=25 and its relative standing IMPROVES with data
hypothesis: At ~200 parameters on the Feynman I.12.2 Coulomb law F = q1*q2/(4*pi*eps*r^2), a KAN is more sample-efficient than iso-parameter MLPs - lower test RMSE at every training-set size, with the gap WIDENING as n shrinks - and its learned edge functions can be snapped back to the true multiplicative formula.
question: Does the KAN's advertised sample efficiency actually hold on the one task family (symbolic formula representation) where KAN is uncontested, once you sweep training-set size and sweep the MLP baseline's shape - and is the true formula genuinely recovered or only approximately fit?
method: Two arms on synthetic seeded data from Feynman I.12.2 (q1,q2,eps,r ~ U[1,5], AI-Feynman benchmark ranges; fixed 2000-point test set, seed 999, std(y_test)=0.0854). (1) SAMPLE-EFFICIENCY SWEEP: real pykan 0.2.8 KAN [4,4,1] grid=5 k=3 (200 trainable spline params) trained with full-batch LBFGS (60 steps, grid updates stopped at step 20, lamb=0) against iso-parameter tanh MLPs 4-11-11-1 and 4-33-1 (199 params each), EACH trained with both full-batch LBFGS (60 steps) and Adam (2000 steps, lr 3e-3). n in {25,50,100,250,500,1000} x 3 data seeds; X and y z-scored with TRAIN statistics only, RMSE reported in original units. The headline MLP baseline is the ORACLE best-of-4 MLP arms per n, deliberately giving the baseline a model-selection advantage the KAN does not get, so the test is conservative w.r.t. the KAN hypothesis. (2) SYMBOLIC ARM: a separate KAN [4,1,1] (the shape the true formula needs: sum of logs into one exp) on RAW un-standardized data at n=1000, grid 5 refined to grid 10, best of 4 init seeds selected on TRAINING loss only; then pykan auto_symbolic over {x,x^2,x^3,1/x,1/x^2,sqrt,exp,log,tanh,sin,abs}, affine refit, symbolic_formula(). Fidelity is scored objectively rather than by eye: OLS of log(F_pred) on (log q1, log q2, log eps, log r) over the test set, which returns (1,1,-1,-2) with R^2=1 for a true monomial; verdict thresholds declared in experiment.yaml. Each layer-0 edge is additionally regressed against a primitive library (log, x, x^2, 1/x, 1/x^2, sqrt, and an exp family scanned over an inner scale, since exp(b*x) is not an affine reparametrization of exp(x)).
architecture: pykan 0.2.8 KAN [4,4,1] grid 5 k 3 (200 spline params) for the sweep; KAN [4,1,1] grid 5->10 for symbolic extraction; iso-param tanh MLPs 4-11-11-1 and 4-33-1 (199 params)

dataset.name: Feynman I.12.2 (Coulomb's law) synthetic, 25-1000 train / 2000 test
dataset.source: generated in run.py from the closed-form equation with AI-Feynman benchmark ranges U[1,5]

task: regression / symbolic formula representation and recovery
compute: CPU single-threaded, 496s total (sweep 353s over 90 fits, symbolic arm 141s)

metrics.formula_fidelity: exact (monomial recovered up to a constant factor)
metrics.headline: Split verdict. SYMBOLIC: exact - pykan's auto_symbolic prints 144.09*(9.18*q1+0.377)^1.0153*(0.0566*q2+0.0004)^1.0031 / ((9.844*eps-0.108)^0.9949*(9.792*r+0.161)^2.0215), i.e. Coulomb's law up to a constant; log-log exponent recovery [0.994, 0.996, -0.996, -2.002] vs true [1,1,-1,-2] (max error 0.006, R^2 0.99999), all four layer-0 edges are log(x) at R^2 0.9997-1.0000 and the output edge is exp at R^2 1.0000, and symbolic snapping cuts test RMSE 32x (0.00549 -> 0.000174, 10x better than the best MLP anywhere in the sweep). SAMPLE EFFICIENCY: refuted - the 200-param KAN beats the oracle best-of-4 iso-param MLP at only 1 of 6 training sizes (n=250, by 6%), is 2.82x WORSE at n=25 (RMSE 0.105 vs 0.037, i.e. at the predict-the-mean floor of 0.085), and ratio(n=25)/ratio(n=1000)=1.86, so its relative standing IMPROVES with data - the opposite of a sample-efficiency advantage. Against a single fixed MLP shape (4-11-11-1 LBFGS) the KAN does win from n=100 up (0.90/0.61/0.77/0.85), so the familiar KAN-beats-MLP plot reproduces only if the baseline's width is never swept.

result_summary: The two halves of the KAN pitch come apart on the same equation. Symbolic recovery is EXACT and better than advertised: a 4-input, 1-hidden-node pykan model trained on 1000 raw points learns log on all four input edges (R^2 0.9997-1.0000; note that scoring the output edge against a*exp(x)+b without an inner scale gives only R^2 0.55 and would have been a false negative - allowing exp(b*x) gives R^2 1.0000 at b=2.33), auto_symbolic prints 144.09*(9.18*q1+0.377)^1.0153*(0.0566*q2+0.0004)^1.0031/((9.844*eps-0.108)^0.9949*(9.792*r+0.161)^2.0215), and an objective log-log regression recovers exponents [0.994, 0.996, -0.996, -2.002] against the true [1, 1, -1, -2] (max error 0.006, R^2 0.99999). Snapping to symbols is also a huge regularizer we did not set out to test: it cuts the same model's test RMSE from 0.00549 to 0.000174 (32x), 10x better than the best MLP at any n. Sample efficiency is REFUTED, and refuted in the worst place for the claim. Against an oracle best-of-4 iso-param MLP baseline (two shapes x two optimizers, per-n oracle selection - an advantage the KAN is not given), the 200-param KAN wins at 1 of 6 training sizes (n=250, by 6%). At n=25 it is 2.82x worse (0.1052 vs 0.0373) and sits at the predict-the-mean floor (std(y_test)=0.0854), i.e. it has learned essentially nothing while a 199-param MLP is already at 0.0373. ratio(n=25)/ratio(n=1000) = 1.86: the KAN's relative position improves with more data. The mechanism is in the method - a B-spline edge is a LOCAL basis, so with 25 points spread over [1,5]^4 most knots see almost no data, whereas an MLP's global tanh features are constrained everywhere by every point; splines need samples per knot, which is a sample-efficiency tax at small n repaid only once the grid is populated. Two reproduction warnings fall out: (1) sweep the MLP's shape - against a single fixed 4-11-11-1 MLP the KAN wins from n=100 up (ratios 0.90/0.61/0.77/0.85), so the familiar plot reproduces if you never vary the baseline's width, but the wide 4-33-1 MLP is the best model overall at n>=500; (2) sweep KAN inits - in pre-run probes the four [4,1,1] init seeds spanned test RMSE 0.0014-0.0126 (9x) at n=1000 and one init at n=400 landed at train MSE 0.70, no better than the mean, so run.py selects over 4 inits by TRAINING loss. Caveats: one equation (a pure monomial, which is the best case for the log/exp decomposition a KAN can express in two layers), 4 variables rather than the backlog's suggested 2-3, ~200 params, 3 data seeds, one KAN init seed in the sweep arm, iso-parameter (not iso-FLOP) matching, and a fixed 60-step LBFGS budget for both families. MLP numbers are bit-identical across runs; the pykan arm is not - two runs of the script differed by <6% in KAN RMSE (KAN won 2/6 vs 1/6 sizes) with no conclusion changed.

title: MQAR at ~0.1M params: attention holds 1.00 recall at every KV load to 24 while a decay-gated linear-attention mixer and a routing-free gated conv both sit ON the no-recall guessing baseline - the 'graceful capacity slide' is chance, not capacity
hypothesis: On hand-rolled MQAR at ~0.1M params, softmax attention holds >=90% recall at every KV load while a decay-gated linear-attention mixer degrades as load grows and a gated long-convolution (no content-based routing) fails hardest; the fresh question is the SHAPE of the linear mixer's failure - a sharp capacity cliff at a load threshold, or a graceful slide.
question: At matched parameters and matched steps on a CPU time-box, does the zoology recall ranking (attention >> sub-quadratic) reproduce at nano scale, and is the sub-quadratic mixer's failure a sharp capacity cliff at a load threshold or a graceful degradation?
method: Hand-rolled MQAR after zoology (repo deliberately NOT cloned - its mamba_ssm/causal-conv1d/fla extras need CUDA). Fixed 52-token context: [k1 v1 ... kN vN][PAD ...][q1 q2 q3 q4]; keys are tokens 0-31, values 32-63, PAD 64 (vocab 65); keys distinct within a sequence, values i.i.d., the 4 query keys a distinct subset of the N present keys; loss and accuracy ONLY at the 4 query positions; values re-randomised per sequence so nothing is memorisable across sequences. Context length and query count held FIXED, only N varies, slack is PAD. Three mixers drop into an identical 2-layer pre-LN residual block (d_model 64, 4 heads, learned absolute PE): (a) attn = causal multi-head softmax attention; (b) gla = decay-gated linear attention in parallel form, A[t,s] = <phi(q_t),phi(k_s)>*exp(c_t-c_s) with phi=elu+1, per-head input-dependent scalar decay gate sigmoid(w_g.x_t), cumulative log-decay c, sum-normalised, SiLU output gate, decay biases init RetNet-style to 1-2^-(3+head); masking is applied BEFORE the exp (masking after overflows and NaNs the backward pass); (c) gconv = gated long depthwise causal convolution proj(u * conv(v)) with a learned full-context per-channel kernel - multiplicative gating but no content-based routing. ISO-PARAM: d_ff binary-searched per mixer to hit 100k params (212/179/218 -> 99880/100078/99892, spread 0.198%). ISO-STEP: 3000 steps, batch 64, AdamW lr 3e-3 (100-step warmup), wd 0.01, grad-clip 1.0 for every mixer; no run hit the time cap. CURRICULUM (deviation forced by the time-box): ONE model per mixer trained on a uniform mixture of loads N ~ U{1..24}, then evaluated separately at loads {1,2,4,8,12,16,20,24} on byte-identical held-out sets of 256 sequences. Crucially the metrics also carry three QUERY-IGNORING no-recall baselines per load (uniformly random value present in context / mode of present values / most recent value) and the per-mixer margin over the best of them, because a model can score far above 1/vocab with no matching at all.
architecture: 2-layer pre-LN residual stack, d_model 64, 4 heads, learned APE, iso-param FFN width per mixer; mixer swapped among softmax attention / decay-gated linear attention (RetNet-GLA flavoured, pure PyTorch) / gated long depthwise causal conv; ~0.1M params each

metrics.cliff_or_graceful: neither - the sub-quadratic curves ARE the no-recall baseline
metrics.headline: At 0.1M params, iso-param (0.198% spread) and iso-step (3000 steps, batch 64), softmax attention reaches 1.000 recall at EVERY KV load 1-24 (whole-sequence exact match 1.000 too), breaking through in a clean phase transition at step ~1250. The decay-gated linear-attention mixer and the routing-free gated conv both fall to 0.52/0.29/0.19/0.09 at loads 2/4/8/24 - but so does the best QUERY-IGNORING baseline (0.53/0.30/0.21/0.13), so the gla margin over that baseline is NEGATIVE at every load >=2 (worst -0.037) and gconv's peak margin is +0.003. Whole-sequence exact match for both is 0.000 at every load >=4. First load below 90%: attn never, gla 2, gconv 2. The backlog's cliff-vs-graceful question is ill-posed at this budget: the smooth ~1/N decay is the guessing floor, not a capacity curve, and the mixer WITH content-based routing is indistinguishable from the one without.

result_summary: The zoology ranking reproduces at nano scale and the fresh question dissolves. Under a strict iso-parameter (99,880 / 100,078 / 99,892 params, 0.198% spread, achieved by binary-searching d_ff per mixer) and iso-step (3000 steps, batch 64, identical optimiser) control, 2-layer softmax attention reaches 1.000 recall accuracy at every KV load from 1 to 24 - and 1.000 whole-sequence exact match, i.e. all four queries correct on all 256 held-out sequences at every load - learning it as a clean phase transition (acc at load 24: 0.094 at step 1000, 0.643 at 1250, 0.855 at 1500, 0.939 at 1750, 1.000 by 2500). The hand-rolled decay-gated linear-attention mixer (elu+1 features, per-head input-dependent scalar decay gate, parallel cumulative-log-decay form, SiLU output gate, RetNet-style decay init) collapses to 0.523/0.291/0.190/0.094 at loads 2/4/8/24, and the routing-free gated long conv to 0.532/0.289/0.195/0.104. Read naively that is a textbook graceful degradation. It is not. The run also computes three query-IGNORING baselines per load; the best of them is 0.529/0.297/0.208/0.126 at those same loads, which means the gla mixer's margin over the no-recall baseline is NEGATIVE at every load >= 2 (-0.006/-0.006/-0.019/-0.037/-0.016/-0.007/-0.032) and gconv's best margin anywhere is +0.003, versus attention's +0.874 at load 24. Whole-sequence exact match for both sub-quadratic mixers is 0.000 at every load >= 4. So neither sub-quadratic model learned any associative recall: both learned only 'emit a value token that occurs in this context', and the apparently smooth ~1/N decay in both rows is that guessing floor. The backlog asked whether the linear mixer's failure is a sharp capacity cliff or a graceful slide; the answer at this budget is neither - it never gets on the curve, and the mixer WITH content-based routing is statistically indistinguishable from the one with none. The practical lesson generalises past this item: plot the query-ignoring baseline before reading a capacity shape off a recall-vs-load sweep, because the chance floor of MQAR is itself a smooth decreasing function of load and will impersonate one. The honest boundary is compute, not capacity: this is iso-STEP, and the gla state (4 heads x 16 x 16 = 1024 scalars) is not obviously too small for 24 pairs, so the supported claim is that the linear mixer fails to LEARN recall in the budget where attention learns it in ~1250 steps, not that it cannot represent it; separating those needs a 10-50x longer run. Two method findings cost most of the day and generalise: (1) batch size is the binding constraint on recall-circuit formation - at batch 16 NO mixer including attention left chance in 10,000 steps, at batch 64 attention broke through in ~1250; (2) embedding init is load-bearing - the GPT-standard std 0.02 on both embedding tables stalls MQAR while nn.Embedding's default std 1.0 solves load 4 in ~750 steps, presumably because the previous-token head needs the position signal to be comparable in scale to the token signal. Caveats: one seed; ONE gla design (sum-normalised elu+1 is one point in a space where DeltaNet's delta rule, Based's Taylor features and larger head dims are all known to help recall), so this is evidence about this mixer, not about gated linear attention in general; the curriculum (train on a uniform mixture of loads 1-24, evaluate per load) is a deviation from a per-load training sweep forced by the time-box, because in pilots a model trained on a single fixed load N>=8 never left chance in 10k steps for any mixer while fixed N=4 was solved in ~750 steps, and we did not disentangle whether that fixed-load solution is positional; iso-step is not iso-wall-clock (attn 236s, gla 375s, gconv 197s); loads stop at 24 because the context is 52 tokens.

title: Weight decay and the grokking delay on (a+b) mod 59: monotone where it groks (1825 -> 750 steps for WD 1 -> 3) but the window is only ~1 decade wide, and WD never touches memorization speed
hypothesis: Weight decay controls the memorize->generalize (grokking) delay: steps-to-grok decreases monotonically as weight decay increases, until a weight decay so high that it destabilizes training (the model can no longer even fit the training set), at which point generalization is lost entirely.
question: Is steps-to-grok really a monotone decreasing function of AdamW weight decay, how wide is the weight-decay window in which grokking happens at all, and does high weight decay kill generalization by degrading the grokked solution or by preventing memorization in the first place?
method: Weight-decay sweep at fixed everything else. 1-layer transformer (no LayerNorm, no biases) on [a, b, '='], logits read at the last position only, d_model 64 / 4 heads / d_mlp 256 / vocab 60, 56,960 params - byte-for-byte the architecture of the sibling run 2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition so the WD=1.0 arm is a direct cross-check. Task: all 59^2 = 3481 pairs of (a+b) mod 59, deterministic random 50/50 split (1740 train / 1741 test, chance 1/59 = 0.017). Full-batch AdamW, lr 1e-3, betas (0.9, 0.98), seed 0, eval every 25 steps. Swept variable: AdamW DECOUPLED weight decay in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0, 10.0, 30.0}, three orders of magnitude around the WD=1.0 of Nanda et al. Per arm we record step_memorized (first train acc >= 0.99), steps_to_grok (first test acc >= 0.95), grok_delay = the difference, best/final test accuracy, accuracy at a COMMON step 1200, and the L2 norm of all parameters at memorization, at the grok step and at the end. Every arm shares a 3000-step cap; arms that never reach test acc 0.95 are reported as CENSORED (steps_to_grok > 3000) rather than dropped, which still adjudicates monotonicity by rank. Arms stop early only after a CONFIRMED grok (grok step + 200 steps) or after 500 steps of failing to fit train, and no arm may stop before step 1200 so that the common-step comparison exists for all of them. Monotonicity is scored by Spearman rank correlation, computed both over the whole sweep and over the arms at or below the best-performing weight decay, with censored arms scored at cap+1 (a lower bound on their true steps-to-grok, so the rank statistic stays valid).
architecture: 1-layer attention+MLP transformer, no LayerNorm, no biases, d_model 64, 4 heads, d_mlp 256, vocab 60, 56,960 params

metrics.seed1_skipped_reason: seed-0 sweep consumed 718s of the 720s budget; all 7 seed-1 arms were skipped and the skips are logged in train.log
metrics.failure_mode_low_wd: cannot generalize (train acc 1.000, test acc plateaus at 0.47-0.50 = 28x chance, censored > 3000 steps)

sibling_crosscheck.note: two independently written runners, same architecture and split protocol, agree to within one 25-step eval interval

metrics.headline: Both halves of the hypothesis hold, but the usable window is ~1 decade wide. Among the arms that grokked, steps-to-grok is strictly decreasing in weight decay: 1825 steps (delay 1600) at WD=1.0 -> 750 steps (delay 500) at WD=3.0, a 2.4x / 3.2x speed-up for a 3x increase in WD, Spearman rho = -0.894 over the arms at or below the optimum. But only 2 of 7 arms spanning three decades grok at all inside a 3000-step cap: WD <= 0.3 memorizes just as fast (step 200) and then sits on a 0.47-0.50 test-accuracy plateau for the whole budget (censored > 3000), while WD >= 10 destabilizes - at WD=10 train accuracy never passes 0.73 and decays to 0.64, and at WD=30 training collapses to chance (train 0.028) with the parameter norm crushed from 23.8 to 7.3. Best test accuracy is a clean inverted U: 0.475, 0.484, 0.501, 0.978, 1.000, 0.593, 0.033. The single cleanest number is that weight decay does not touch memorization at all - step_memorized is 200/200/200/225/250 across a 100x range of WD, so everything weight decay does, it does after the training set is already fit. Grokking coincides with a weight-norm band: the two grokking arms crossed at ||theta|| = 34.0 and 31.8, memorize-only arms end above it (50.5/46.4/40.8) and cannot-fit arms end below it (19.5/7.3).

result_summary: A 7-point weight-decay sweep spanning three orders of magnitude (0.03 to 30) on a 57k-param 1-layer transformer at p=59, train_frac 0.5, one seed, 3000-step cap, 718s of CPU. BOTH halves of the hypothesis survive, but the honest headline is that the grokking window is narrow. (1) MONOTONE WHERE IT GROKS: only WD=1.0 and WD=3.0 reach test acc 0.95 inside the cap, and among them steps-to-grok is strictly decreasing - 1825 -> 750 steps, delay 1600 -> 500 - i.e. 2.4x faster to grok and 3.2x shorter delay for a 3x larger WD (Spearman rho(WD, steps-to-grok) = -0.894 over arms at or below the optimum, but only -0.178 over the whole sweep, because the top end reverses). (2) DESTABILIZATION IS REAL AND SHARP: at WD=10 the model NEVER memorizes (train acc peaks at 0.73, decays to 0.64) and test accuracy stalls at 0.59; at WD=30 it collapses outright (train 0.028, test 0.027 vs chance 0.017) with the parameter norm crushed 23.8 -> 7.3 instead of being allowed to grow. Best test accuracy across the sweep is a clean inverted U: 0.475 / 0.484 / 0.501 / 0.978 / 1.000 / 0.593 / 0.033. (3) THE SHARPEST RESULT WE DID NOT SET OUT TO GET: weight decay has NO effect on memorization speed. step_memorized is 200, 200, 200, 225, 250 across a 100x range of WD - everything weight decay does, it does after the training set is fit. (4) A WEIGHT-NORM BAND SEPARATES THE THREE REGIMES: peak ||theta|| falls monotonically with WD (50.8, 48.7, 45.7, 41.2, 34.5, 23.8, 23.8); the two grokking arms crossed the threshold at ||theta|| = 34.0 and 31.8; memorize-but-never-grok arms end ABOVE that band (50.5 / 46.4 / 40.8) and cannot-fit arms end BELOW it (19.5 / 7.3). Grokking happens exactly when WD is strong enough to pull the norm down to ~30-34 but not so strong that the norm cannot rise to fit the data first. (5) CROSS-CHECK PASSES: the WD=1.0 arm reproduces the sibling run 2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition (independently written, same architecture and split protocol) to within one 25-step eval interval - memorization 225 vs 220, test-acc-0.5 crossing 875 vs 862, delay 650 vs 642. CAVEATS, worst first: ONE SEED - the budget was written to run a second seed on whatever arms fit after the seed-0 sweep, but the sweep used 718s of the 720s budget and all 7 seed-1 arms were skipped (logged in train.log), so every arm is n=1 and the sibling cross-check is the only independent evidence. CENSORING IS A BUDGET ARTIFACT: prior art (arXiv:2605.20441) puts the true critical weight decay near 0.016, below our smallest arm, so the WD <= 0.3 arms would most likely grok eventually; this experiment shows only that they do not inside 3000 steps while WD=3 does it in 750, so the monotone claim is supported as 'decreasing in WD', not as a measurement of how long the slow arms take. THE PLATEAU IS NOT A PURE MEMORIZATION PLATEAU: at train_frac 0.5 the non-grokking arms sit at ~0.48 test accuracy, 28x chance, so they have learned real structure; the classic memorize-at-chance plateau needs a smaller train fraction than fits a 12-minute box. Also one modulus, one architecture, one learning rate - AdamW's decoupled shrink is lr*wd per step, so this is a slice at lr=1e-3, not a WD axis in general.

novelty_check.conclusion: Direct prior art exists and was read: arXiv:2605.20441 (Weight Decay Regimes in Grokking Transformers) sweeps lambda in {0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 10.0} at p=97 on a 4-layer/8-head/d_model-128 (0.82M param) transformer at 50% train with 10-30 seeds, and reports the SAME three-regime structure we find: memorization below a critical lambda_c ~ 0.0158, time-to-grok falling ~1090 -> ~83 epochs over lambda in [0.1, 2.0], and collapse at lambda = 10 (power-law exponent nu = 0.757). Our result agrees with it at 1/14 the parameter count on one CPU thread, so the delay-vs-WD curve itself is NOT novel and is not claimed as such. The backlog's listed prior art, github.com/teddykoker/grokking, was fetched and is a reproduction of the Power et al. curve with no weight-decay sweep. arXiv:2602.02859 ('anti-grokking') is a DIFFERENT phenomenon - a late-stage test-accuracy collapse AFTER generalization, which that paper finds weight decay SUPPRESSES, whereas our high-WD arms fail before ever memorizing. What this run adds on top of 2605.20441: (a) the cheapest check of the three-regime picture we know of - 57k params, 7 arms, 12 CPU-minutes; (b) the sweep extended to lambda = 30, where the parameter norm is actively crushed 23.8 -> 7.3 rather than merely stalled; (c) the two failure modes separated by an explicit metric, 'cannot generalize' (lambda <= 0.3: train 1.000, test 0.48) vs 'cannot memorize' (lambda >= 10: train 0.639 / 0.028); (d) the observation that step_memorized is invariant (200-250) across the entire usable range of lambda, so weight decay acts only on the post-memorization delay; and (e) explicit censoring of non-grokking arms instead of dropping them.

title: Test-time compute on a 0.06M-param weight-tied loop: trained at a FIXED K=3 the loop degrades past its trained depth (frontier acc 1.00 -> 0.55, easy instances 1.00 -> 0.71); trained with a STOCHASTIC depth schedule the identical model extrapolates to 2.67x the trained depth (0.85 at K=8, 11x full-sequence exact match)
hypothesis: A weight-tied looped block trained at K=3 loop iterations on a task whose difficulty is exactly the number of required sequential steps (prefix-parity under a 2-token attention window, where difficulty d needs K >= d-1) learns a REUSABLE one-step propagation rule, so running K > 3 at test time monotonically raises accuracy on harder instances instead of degrading it - and an untied depth-3 baseline with 2.6x the parameters cannot extend at all.
question: Does a weight-tied loop actually trade TEST-TIME compute for accuracy - i.e. does running more loop iterations at inference than at training improve accuracy on harder (deeper) instances - or does it degrade past K_train, which is the common failure? And if the axis exists at all, what decides which of the two you get?
method: The task is engineered so that test-time compute is the ONLY currency that buys accuracy. Prefix-parity (cumulative XOR): input [BOS, x_1..x_L] with x_i in {0,1}, target y_i = XOR(x_1..x_i). Attention is banded causal with WINDOW 1 - every position attends only to itself and its immediate predecessor - so after K applications of the block position i can only have seen bits [i-K, i], and difficulty d (= position index) is solvable IFF K >= d-1. There is no shallow heuristic and no parameter count that substitutes for a loop iteration; an ideal extrapolator sits at 1.00 on the analytically known frontier d = K+1 for every K, and a model that cannot reuse its own rule sits at chance 0.50 the moment d > K_train+1. Architecture: pre-LN transformer block, d_model 64, 2 heads, d_ff 256, NoPE (BOS token + the band supply all positional structure), final LayerNorm + 2-way linear readout; 58,370 params tied (50,178 without the injection adapter), 149,634 params for the untied depth-3 control (2.6x). Train: K=3, L ~ U{1..4} (exactly what 3 loops covers), AdamW lr 2e-3 wd 0.01, batch 256, 1500 steps, grad-clip 1.0, 100-step warmup. Test: K in {1..8} on 1024 held-out length-9 sequences at a fixed eval seed; because attention is causal, per-position accuracy on ONE length-9 batch yields every difficulty d=1..9 at once, giving a full accuracy(test K, difficulty) matrix. Four arms x 3 seeds = 12 runs: (1) tied_fixK3_inj - the backlog's literal spec, tied block at fixed K=3 with recurrent-depth-style per-iteration input injection (adapter on [h ; e]); (2) tied_fixK3_noinj - vanilla loop, no injection, the variant 2026-07-25_shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop flagged as its caveat; (3) tied_randK_inj - identical to (1) but trained with a STOCHASTIC depth schedule, k ~ U{1,2,3} per batch with L = k+1 so every supervised position is computable at the sampled depth (still never sees K>3 or L>4); (4) untied_d3 - 3 independent blocks evaluated once, plus two ad-hoc extensions it has no right to (repeat-last-block, cycle-blocks 0,1,2,0,1,2). Headline metric is FRONTIER ACCURACY = acc[K][d=K+1], the accuracy at the deepest difficulty K iterations could possibly solve, scored against ground truth rather than against another model.
architecture: weight-tied pre-LN transformer block, banded causal attention (window 1), NoPE, d_model 64 / 2 heads / d_ff 256, 58,370 params tied (50,178 no-injection) vs 149,634 untied depth-3

metrics.headline: The hypothesis as stated is REFUTED and the repair is decisive. Frontier accuracy (accuracy at difficulty d = K+1, the deepest instance K loops could possibly solve; chance 0.50, ideal 1.00): the backlog's literal arm tied_fixK3_inj runs 0.67 / 0.71 / 1.00 / 0.66 / 0.64 / 0.59 / 0.59 / 0.55 over K = 1..8 - perfect at the trained depth, then monotone DECAY, and the damage is not confined to hard instances: mean accuracy on the easy trained-depth difficulties (d <= 4) falls 1.000 -> 0.713 simply by running 8 loops instead of 3. Zero of 5 hard difficulties are monotone in K. The identical architecture and parameter count trained with a STOCHASTIC depth schedule (k ~ U{1,2,3}, L = k+1; still never sees K>3 or L>4) runs 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.96 / 0.95 / 0.89 / 0.87 / 0.85 - it tracks the ideal frontier out to K=8, 2.67x its trained depth, at a difficulty where every other arm is at chance. Full-sequence exact match on all 9 positions (requires 8 correct sequential steps) goes 0.038 at K=3 -> 0.428 at K=8, an 11x gain purely from test-time compute, vs 0.056 / 0.080 / 0.026 for the other three arms. All 3 seeds separate cleanly (0.77/0.83/0.95 vs 0.47/0.51/0.67). The untied depth-3 control with 2.6x the params matches every tied arm in-distribution (1.00 on d<=4 at K=3) and is at chance for every d>4 at every K; two ad-hoc extensions are exactly null (cycling leaves K=4 and K=5 bit-identical to K=3). Mechanism note: the failure is computational drift, not numerical blow-up - tied_fixK3_inj's residual norm is BOUNDED (9.4 -> 8.7 over 8 iterations) while it collapses, and tied_fixK3_noinj blows up 6.6x (13.7 -> 90.7) while staying the second most stable arm, because without input injection the loop converges to a FIXED POINT (rows K=4..8 nearly identical) - safe because it computes nothing new, and it never solves a single difficulty beyond d=4.

result_summary: The direct test of the 'test-time-compute axis' that 2026-07-25_shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop said the loop must earn its place on. Task built so the axis exists at all: prefix-parity with a WINDOW-1 banded causal attention, which makes difficulty d (= position index) solvable iff K >= d-1, so required sequential steps EQUAL difficulty and the ideal frontier d = K+1 is known analytically. 58k-param tied block, 3 seeds, 4 arms, 617s of one CPU thread. Every arm converges (train loss <= 5e-5) and every arm is perfect in-distribution (1.00 on d<=4 at K=3), so in-distribution fit is nowhere a confound. (1) THE BACKLOG'S LITERAL SETUP FAILS IN THE PREDICTED WAY. Trained at a fixed K=3, frontier accuracy is 1.00 at the trained depth and then decays to 0.55 at K=8; extra loops also corrupt instances the model had ALREADY solved, with mean accuracy on d<=4 falling 1.000 -> 0.713. None of the 5 hard difficulties is monotone in K. On this model, running more loops than you trained is strictly worse than stopping. (2) A STOCHASTIC DEPTH SCHEDULE FLIPS IT COMPLETELY. Same architecture, same 58,370 params, same 1500 steps, and still never more than 3 loops or 4 tokens in training - but sampling k ~ U{1,2,3} with L = k+1 yields 1.00/1.00/1.00/0.96/0.95/0.89/0.87/0.85 across K=1..8, i.e. real extrapolation to 2.67x the trained depth. Per difficulty, accuracy at the required K vs at K_train: d5 0.956 vs 0.503, d6 0.953 vs 0.509, d7 0.889 vs 0.503, d8 0.872 vs 0.497, d9 0.849 vs 0.505. Full-sequence exact match on all 9 positions rises 0.038 -> 0.428 (11x) purely from test-time compute; the other arms manage 0.056 / 0.080 / 0.026. All three seeds of the stochastic arm extrapolate (0.77/0.83/0.95 at K=8) and all three of the fixed-K arm fail (0.47/0.51/0.67) - no overlap. (3) THE UNTIED CONTROL CANNOT EXTEND AND NO HACK RESCUES IT. untied_d3 has 2.6x the parameters and ties every tied arm in-distribution, but its MAXIMUM accuracy anywhere in the entire d>4, K>3 region of the matrix is 0.511 - it never leaves chance, not once, in 40 cells. Repeating the last block gets d=5 to 0.501 at K=4; cycling blocks 0,1,2,0,1,2 leaves rows K=4 and K=5 bit-identical to K=3 and then degrades. Depth you did not tie is depth you cannot spend later. (4) THE FIXED-K FAILURE IS COMPUTATIONAL DRIFT, NOT NUMERICAL BLOW-UP. Residual-stream norm over 8 iterations: tied_fixK3_inj 9.4 -> 8.7 (bounded, and it collapses anyway) vs tied_fixK3_noinj 13.7 -> 90.7 (6.6x blow-up, and it is the SECOND MOST STABLE arm on easy instances, 1.000 -> 0.950). Norm growth and accuracy degradation are anti-correlated here. (5) INPUT INJECTION IS WHAT LETS A LOOP MOVE - AND THEREFORE BREAK. Without injection the loop converges to a fixed point (rows K=4..8 nearly identical, 1.00/1.00/0.91/0.91/0.65/...): extra loops are safe precisely because they compute nothing new, and it never solves a single difficulty beyond d=4. With injection the state keeps moving, which is the precondition both for extrapolation (arm 3) and for collapse (arm 1); the depth schedule alone decides which. IMPLICATION FOR SHADOW: this is the first axis on which the loop has earned anything, and it retro-explains three sibling nulls - shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop, shadow-recursion-capacity-window and shadow-halt-entropy-tiny ALL trained at fixed loop counts, which this run identifies as exactly the configuration in which the loop's one advantage does not exist. The ledger entry should read: tie the block, train the depth stochastically, or do not loop at all. It also explains why entropy halting was useless - an adaptive-depth policy needs a model whose quality varies usefully with depth, and a fixed-K-trained loop does not have one. CAVEATS, WORST FIRST. (a) THE TASK IS DESIGNED TO REWARD LOOPING: window-1 attention makes required steps exactly equal difficulty, the friendliest possible arena, and says nothing about whether natural-language difficulty has this structure (shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop suggests it does not). (b) One task, one architecture, one width, 3 seeds, 1500 steps. (c) The extrapolation is good but not perfect - 0.85 at K=8, decaying gently (0.96/0.95/0.89/0.87/0.85), so it presumably dies somewhere past K ~ 15; we did not find that point. (d) The stochastic arm differs from the fixed arm in TWO ways at once (random k AND the coupled L = k+1), so 'stochastic depth' here is the schedule as a package, not k-randomization alone. (e) Two metrics in results.json are brittle and are not the result: deepest_solved demands >= 95% on EVERY prefix, so a single 0.92 zeroes it and it badly under-reports the stochastic arm; and the strict 'nondecreasing' flag in monotonicity_by_arm fires false for the stochastic arm too, but only because of sub-1% jitter between chance-level cells (its d=5 runs 0.503 -> 0.509 -> 0.503 -> 0.956 over K=1..4). frontier_acc_by_arm is the metric to read. (f) Shrunk to a ~12-minute CPU box versus the backlog's ~1.5 hr estimate: 0.06M params, 1500 steps, lengths <= 9.

novelty_check.conclusion: Direct prior art exists and was read. arXiv:2606.29983 ('Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping') is the closest: on binary addition / Dyck-1 / Unique-Set / Copy with a looped 3-layer block trained on lengths < 20 and tested on lengths >= 20, it reports that fixed-loop-depth training produces runs with matched in-distribution accuracy but qualitatively different OOD behaviour (binary addition at fixed K=20: 34.2% OOD accuracy, std 7.4 across runs) and that SAMPLING THE LOOP COUNT during training substantially reduces that variance - the same mechanism our arm-1-vs-arm-3 contrast isolates, so the stochastic-depth fix is REPLICATED, not claimed as new. arXiv:2409.15647 (Looped Transformers for Length Generalization, UW-Madison, the backlog's listed prior art) establishes that looped transformers with an adaptive number of steps length-generalize on arithmetic and algorithmic tasks including parity. arXiv:2502.05171 (recurrent depth) is the source of the per-iteration input injection used here and of the test-time-compute framing, and also trains with a randomized recurrence count. WHAT THIS RUN ADDS: (i) SCALE - 58,370 parameters, 4 arms x 3 seeds, 617 s on ONE CPU thread, the cheapest demonstration of the effect we are aware of and cheap enough to serve as a regression test; (ii) the task is constructed so required sequential steps EQUAL the difficulty axis, which converts the usual single OOD-accuracy scalar into a 2-D accuracy(test K, difficulty) matrix with an analytically known ideal frontier d = K+1, so extrapolation is scored against ground truth rather than against another model; (iii) the untied-depth control is extended by two explicit hacks (repeat-last-block and cycle-blocks) and measured to be exactly null - prior art asserts untied depth cannot extend but does not quantify it; (iv) the norm-vs-accuracy DISSOCIATION - the arm whose residual norm blows up 6.6x is the stable one, while the norm-bounded arm is the one that collapses, and the no-injection loop is shown to be safe only because it converges to a fixed point - which we did not find reported; (v) direct linkage to the lab's own sibling nulls (shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop, shadow-recursion-capacity-window, shadow-halt-entropy-tiny), all of which trained at fixed loop counts.

title: SAEs on a grokked (a+b) mod 59 transformer: against a provable Fourier ground truth the raw neuron basis is 0.75 frequency-pure and the best usable SAE only 0.32 - the sparsity prior fights the density of the true features
hypothesis: A small overcomplete L1 sparse autoencoder trained on the MLP hidden activations of a fully grokked (a+b) mod 59 transformer will recover the model's known Fourier structure: a large fraction of its alive features will be frequency-pure (>=80% of their 2D Fourier power on a single frequency k) and the set of frequencies claimed by those features will match the model's key frequencies.
question: In the one interpretability setting with a PROVABLE answer key - a grokked modular-addition transformer, which is known to implement Fourier multiplication - do SAE features actually recover the ground-truth Fourier units, are all key frequencies recovered, and how does SAE faithfulness compare against the standard-basis (raw neuron) baseline that everyone skips?
method: No training of the task model: the fully grokked checkpoint (train acc 1.000, test acc 1.000, verified in-run at 1.0000 accuracy on all 3481 pairs) is LOADED from the sibling run 2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition/model.pt, together with its saved key_freqs [24, 17, 5, 3, 6, 25]. Activation site: post-ReLU MLP hidden layer (d_mlp = 256) evaluated on ALL p^2 = 3481 inputs; activations are norm-scaled so E||x|| = sqrt(d) which makes the L1 coefficient comparable across models. SAE: standard ReLU dictionary (f = ReLU((x - b_dec) W_enc + b_enc), x_hat = f W_dec + b_dec), decoder rows renormalised to unit norm every step, L1 penalty on f, Adam lr 3e-3, batch 256, 2500 steps, dead-feature resampling at 40% and 70% of training. Arms: 4x expansion (1024 features) at three sparsity coefficients lambda in {0.3, 1.0, 3.0} on each of three activation sources, plus one extra 8x (2048-feature) grokked arm at lambda = 1.0 = 10 SAEs. GROUND-TRUTH SCORE: build the orthonormal real 2D Fourier basis over (a,b) in Z_59 x Z_59; frequency k's block is the 3x3 span {1, cos w_k a, sin w_k a} x {1, cos w_k b, sin w_k b} minus DC, and these blocks are disjoint once DC is dropped, so purity = max_k power_k / (total non-DC power) is a genuine partition statistic. A unit is PURE iff purity >= 0.8 and ALIVE iff it fires on >= 1% of the 3481 inputs. Two purity views per feature: (i) activation-map purity, the spectrum of the feature's own firing pattern f(a,b); (ii) decoder-direction purity, the spectrum of w_f . x(a,b) read out by the feature's unit-norm decoder direction - view (ii) ignores the ReLU gate and is deliberately the metric most favourable to the SAE. For a raw neuron the two coincide. FOUR CONTROLS: (1) the raw 256 MLP neurons scored with the identical metric (the head-to-head baseline); (2) SAEs on model_mid.pt, the memorized-not-generalizing checkpoint (test acc 0.102); (3) SAEs on a random-init transformer of the same architecture; (4) random-unit-direction and random-sparse-indicator-map nulls for the purity statistic itself. An arm is flagged COLLAPSED (and excluded from the headline, but still reported) if FVU > 0.25 or fewer than 10 features are alive, so that a dead autoencoder cannot claim a trivially perfect purity.
architecture: frozen 1-layer attention+MLP transformer, no LayerNorm, no biases, d_model 64 / 4 heads / d_mlp 256 / vocab 60, 56,960 params (loaded, not trained) + 10 ReLU sparse autoencoders, 4x (1024 feat, 0.53M params) and 8x (2048 feat, 1.05M params) over the 256-dim MLP hidden layer

metrics.reproducibility: two back-to-back runs produced identical results.json apart from per-arm wall-clock fields

result_summary: The hypothesis is REFUTED, and the sharpest number is the baseline nobody runs. Against a provable answer key, the RAW MLP NEURON BASIS of the grokked model is already 0.750 frequency-pure (mean purity 0.827, median 0.9257, 192 of 256 neurons pure) while the best NON-COLLAPSED SAE reaches only 0.318 (8x expansion, lambda=1.0) and the best 4x arm only 0.105. Even the deliberately SAE-friendly decoder-direction metric, which ignores the ReLU gate, peaks at 0.568 - still below the neurons. The SAE does not beat doing nothing. (2) SPARSITY IS THE CAUSE, AND THE PURE LIMIT IS DEGENERATE: purity rises monotonically with the L1 coefficient (0.120 -> 0.334 -> 0.917 mean) but so does FVU (0.009 -> 0.068 -> 0.990). The only arm that is 100% pure explains 1% of the variance with ONE surviving feature out of 1024 - a collapsed autoencoder, not an interpretation. Every arm that actually reconstructs is <= 0.32 pure. The mechanism is structural rather than a tuning failure: a true Fourier feature cos(w_k(a+b)) is DENSE (nonzero almost everywhere on the grid) while L1 rewards features that fire rarely - alive SAE features fire on 6.6-21.7% of inputs against 62.6% for the average neuron, and a localised indicator is spectrally broad by construction. The sparsity prior and the ground-truth feature shape are in direct conflict. (3) NO ARM RECOVERS THE KEY-FREQUENCY SET - BUT NEITHER DO THE NEURONS, AND THAT IS ITSELF A FINDING: the checkpoint's saved key_freqs (top-6 of the EMBEDDING spectrum) are {24, 17, 5, 3, 6, 25}, but the MLP layer only uses FOUR - all 192 pure neurons claim {3, 5, 17, 24}, holding 97.0% of neuron activation power, while freq 25 holds 0.65% and freq 6 holds 0.32%, less than frequency 11 which is not a key freq at all. So the embedding-derived key-frequency set OVER-COUNTS the algorithm the MLP actually runs by two, and any 'did the SAE find all key freqs' test inherits that. The best SAE arm claims a strict SUBSET, {5, 17, 24}, dropping frequency 3 entirely, with 0.911 of its dictionary dead. (4) CONTROLS ALL LAND WHERE THEY SHOULD: SAEs on the memorized-not-generalizing checkpoint are 0.000 pure at every lambda (max mean purity 0.092) and SAEs on a random-init transformer are 0.000 pure; raw neurons of those two models score 0.137 and 0.131 mean purity; random sparse indicator maps score 0.005. The metric is not 'any SAE looks pure' - the grokked model is the only source with recoverable structure and the SAE partially finds it. (5) A CAVEAT THAT CUTS AGAINST OUR OWN SAE-FRIENDLY METRIC: a RANDOM unit direction in the grokked activation space already scores 0.482 mean purity (p99 = 0.80), because that space is spanned by only 4 frequencies, so decoder-direction purity has a high null and the 0.638 mean at lambda=1.0 is a real but modest lift. The activation-map metric has a near-zero null (0.005) and is the honest one - and it is the metric on which the SAE does worst. CAVEATS, worst first: ONE SEED, one model, one site (MLP hidden; the post-attention residual stream was not swept, for budget); only 3 sparsity coefficients and 2 expansions; 2500 SAE steps on a fully-enumerated 3481-point dataset the SAE could in principle memorize; only the plain L1/ReLU SAE was tested, so this says nothing about top-k, JumpReLU or matryoshka variants that decouple L0 from per-feature density - which is exactly the mitigation the density mechanism predicts and the obvious next run; model_mid.pt comes from a different train/test split than model.pt (inherited from the sibling experiment), which does not affect its use here since activations are taken on all p^2 inputs; and the COLLAPSED-arm rule (FVU <= 0.25 and >= 10 alive) is a judgement call, fixed before purity was inspected.

novelty_check.conclusion: Partial prior art on every ingredient, none on the combination. The general claim that SAEs recover plausible-but-non-canonical units is the ICLR 2025 canonical-units critique (openreview HpUs2EXjOl, 'Rethinking Evaluation of Sparse Autoencoders'), listed in the backlog; the Fourier answer key and the frequency-purity style of neuron scoring are Nanda et al. 2301.05217; arXiv:2402.16726 analyses circuits in grokked transformers on modular polynomials but not with SAEs; the SAE recipe is Bricken et al. 'Towards Monosemanticity' / ARENA 3.1; and openreview DSOTgzeH3w ('On the Limits of Sparse Autoencoders: A Theoretical Framework and Reweighted Remedy') gives theory that L1 SAEs are biased against high-density features, which is precisely the mechanism isolated empirically here. To our search, no prior work scores SAE features against the PROVABLE Fourier answer key of a grokked modular-addition transformer with (i) the raw neuron basis as a head-to-head baseline, (ii) memorized and random-init models as negative controls, and (iii) a random-direction null for the purity statistic itself. The three additions are the contribution - in particular the finding that the standard basis BEATS the learned dictionary (0.75 vs 0.32) and that the gap is explained by feature density rather than SAE tuning. The grokked model and the purity metric are replications. Search was web-only (arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this box); the two 2026-dated hits that surfaced were not leaned on for numbers.

title: The merge breakpoint: correlated feature pairs never choose local orthogonality - unequal importance kills the weak member by amplitude decay along the SAME direction, and anticorrelated values only bend the merge to |cos| 0.64-0.75
hypothesis: The pair-merging seen at equal importance in 2026-07-23_superposition-correlation-phase breaks down under two stressors - unequal within-pair importance, and anticorrelated within-pair VALUES - and past some breakpoint the pair abandons its shared direction for a locally orthogonal basis (within-pair |cos| < 0.7).
question: When does pair-merging in the Anthropic toy model become too lossy? Where is the breakpoint in within-pair importance ratio r, or in within-pair value correlation c, at which the merged pair splits into a locally orthogonal basis?
method: Anthropic-style toy autoencoder ReLU(W^T W x + b), n=16 features in 8 pairs -> m=4 dims (80 params), importance-weighted MSE, Adam lr=0.01, 3000 online steps, batch 1024, density fixed at p=0.1, 2 seeds. Three independent within-pair knobs, each an exact mixture construction verified empirically in-run (emp corr within 0.008 of target): (i) INDICATOR correlation rho via the sibling's shared-coin mixture; (ii) VALUE correlation c via a copy/mirror mixture - with prob |c| the partner's value is copied (c>0) or mirrored v2=1-v1 (c<0) from the first member's Uniform[0,1] draw, else independent, so marginals stay uniform and the Pearson correlation of co-active values is exactly c; (iii) IMPORTANCE ratio r with importances (2/(1+r), 2r/(1+r)) so the pair's TOTAL importance is 2 for every r - r is a pure split knob, not a pair-weight knob. Three sweeps, 33 distinct cells / 66 runs (shared cells trained once): A importance r in {1,2,4,8,16,64,256} x rho in {0, 0.75, 1} at c=0, where rho=0 is the UNCORRELATED CONTROL separating merge-abandonment from ordinary low-importance feature dropping; B value correlation c in {+1,+0.5,0,-0.5,-1} x rho in {0.75,1} at r=1; C joint corner r in {1,4,16} x c in {+1,0,-1} at rho=1. Per cell: the sibling's merge metric (mean within-pair |cos| among pairs where BOTH members have ||W_i|| >= 0.5) plus SIGNED cosine, a per-pair classification into MERGED (|cos|>=0.7) / AMBIGUOUS / LOCALLY-ORTHOGONAL (|cos|<=0.3) / DROPPED, column norms, cross-pair |cos|, and held-out per-feature reconstruction MSE on a fresh 8192-sample batch normalised by that feature's variance (1.0 = no better than the best constant predictor).
architecture: linear tied W (4x16) + bias, ReLU output, importance-weighted MSE (~80 params)
